4.35.d: तृप्त्यर्थमन्नं हि मया दत्तं तेषां मुदेस्तु वै .. 13 ..
4.35.m: for their satisfaction indeed food has been given by me; let it be for their joy!"
Having offered the bali to beings in this way, waiting for the duration of a cow-milking
for an arriving guest, he should then enter the dining chamber.
Not having offered the crow-bali, he should perform the daily śrāddha.
In the daily śrāddha, according to his capacity, he should feed three, two,
or even one, for the ancestor sacrifice; if weak, he may set aside [the food] and give it.
The daily śrāddha is devoid of offerings to gods, free from customary restrictions,
devoid of sacrificial fees, and free from the vows of giver and enjoyer.
Having performed the ancestor sacrifice thus, with a calm mind and free from anxiety,
seated upon a clean seat, he should eat together with his children,
fragrant, cheerful, wearing a garland, and clad in two clean garments.
Facing east or facing north, he should eat that which has been offered to the ancestors,
having rendered the food non-naked, above and below,
by performing the water-sipping rite (āpośana); thus the wise twice-born should eat.
He should offer [balis saying] 'To the Lord of the earth!', likewise 'To the Lord of the world!',
and saying 'Svāhā to the Lord of beings!', [he places] three balis on the ground.
And having touched water once, the group of five oblations beginning with prāṇa
he should offer into the fire of the stomach-pit, holding darbha grass in his hand, with a serene mind.

4.35.s: darbhapāṇistu yo bhuṃkte tasya doṣo na vidyate ..
4.35.d: दर्भपाणिस्तु यो भुंक्ते तस्य दोषो न विद्यते ..
4.35.m: For one who eats holding darbha grass in hand, no defect is known;
arising from hair, insects, and the like; therefore he should eat possessing darbha.
He should eat food as long as he desires, and should not speak of its qualities or defects.
The ancestors eat as long as its qualities and defects are not spoken of.

4.35.s: ato maunena yo bhuṃkte sa bhuṃkte kevalāmṛtam ..
4.35.d: अतो मौनेन यो भुंक्ते स भुंक्ते केवलामृतम् ..
4.35.m: Therefore, he who eats in silence eats pure nectar.

4.35.s: anupīya tataḥ kṣīraṃ takraṃ pānīyameva vā .. 25 ..
4.35.d: अनुपीय ततः क्षीरं तक्रं पानीयमेव वा .. 25 ..
4.35.m: Then, having drunk afterward milk, buttermilk, or water,
having sipped water once, saying: 'You are the covering of nectar,'
he should pour out the remainder of the drunk water onto the ground, reciting this mantra:
"From the base of the right thumb of the unwashed hand,
for those residing for myriad millions [of years] in Raurava, the abode of non-merit,
who desire the leftover water, let this remain imperishable!"
Having sipped water once again, the intelligent man, becoming purified with effort,
Taking water in hand, he should recite this mantra:
"The Person, thumb-sized, who resides in the thumb,

4.35.s: īśaḥ sarvasya jagataḥ prabhuḥ prīṇāti viśvabhuk .. 4.1.35.230 ..
4.35.d: ईशः सर्वस्य जगतः प्रभुः प्रीणाति विश्वभुक् .. 4.1.35.230 ..
4.35.m: The Lord of the whole universe, the Master who consumes all, may He be pleased!"
Having thus consecrated the food, and having washed feet and hands,
He should then recite these mantras for the digestion of the food:
"May the fire, nourishing the earthly bodily humors, impelled by the wind,
Given space by the sky, digest [it]—may there be comfort for me!
May there be food-nourishment for the prāṇa, apāna, samāna,
As well as udāna and vyāna, and may my happiness be unimpeded!
May the ocean, the submarine fire, the sun, and the son of the sun—
May these digest all that has been consumed by me without remainder!"
Then, having purified his mouth, [and having passed] the remainder of the day
By hearing the Purāṇas and the like, he should then begin the twilight prayer.

4.35.s: gṛhe goṣṭhe nadītīre saṃdhyā daśaguṇā kramāt ..
4.35.d: गृहे गोष्ठे नदीतीरे संध्या दशगुणा क्रमात् ..
4.35.m: The twilight prayer [performed] in a house, a cow-pen, or on a riverbank is tenfold in succession;
At a confluence it becomes a hundredfold, and truly infinite in the presence of Śiva.
The twilight prayer performed outdoors pacifies the sin
Of daytime sexual intercourse, the sin of false speech, and that born of the smell of liquor.
Whose nature is the Sāmaveda, accompanied by the seer Vasiṣṭha,
Dark-limbed, dressed in black garments, her youth slightly declining,
Sarasvatī, riding on Garuḍa, destroyer of obstacles, having Viṣṇu as her deity,
Endowed with the jagatī meter, the supreme one of a single syllable—he should meditate on her.
And having performed sipping [of water] with the mantra "Agniś ca...", the wise man,
Facing the west, should chant until the stars are visible.
Having honored a guest who arrives in the evening,
Even with words, earth, grass, or water, and having thus spent the first watch of the night, the wise man,
Having thus performed the work of the day through the recitation and teaching of the Veda,
Should lie down, not overly full, upon a bed made of a single piece of wood.
Indeed, this eternal rule has been declared in summary.
Conducting himself in this manner, a brahmin never comes to ruin.

4.35.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāharasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthe kāśīkhaṃḍe pūrvārddhe sadācāro nāma paṃcatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 35 .. ..
4.35.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहरस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंडे पूर्वार्द्धे सदाचारो नाम पंचत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 35 .. ..
4.35.m: Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, named "Right Conduct", in the first half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skandapurāṇa.

4.36.m: Skanda said:
"I will state further particulars of right conduct, O pot-born [Agastya],
Having heard which even an ordinary man becomes wise and does not enter the darkness of ignorance.

4.36.s: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāstrayo varṇā dvijāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
4.36.d: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजाः स्मृताः ..
4.36.m: Brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas—the three classes are known as the twice-born:
First born from the mother, and second from the upanayana.
Their rites are Vedic, beginning with conception and ending at the cremation ground.
The wise man should deposit the semen during the fertile season, avoiding Mūla and Maghā.
Before quickening, the puṃsavana [is done], then the sīmantonnayana

4.36.s: māsi ṣaṣṭhe'ṣṭame vāpi jātetho jātakarma ca .. 4 ..
4.36.d: मासि षष्ठेऽष्टमे वापि जातेथो जातकर्म च .. 4 ..
4.36.m: In the sixth or eighth month; and then, once born, the birth rite (jātakarma).
The naming on the eleventh day; taking out from the house in the fourth month;
The first feeding of food in the sixth month; tonsure in the [third] year, or according to family tradition.
In this way the sin arising from the seed and born of the womb is pacified.
For women, these rites are performed silently, but marriage is accompanied by mantras.
In the seventh or eighth year a brahmin is fit for the Sāvitrī [initiation];
A king in the eleventh, and a vaiśya in the twelfth, or according to family tradition.
For the increase of Vedic radiance, a brahmin is fit in the fifth year;
A king desiring strength should take the muñja-girdle in the sixth, and a vaiśya in the eighth.
And the guru should teach the Veda preceded by the great vyāhṛtis,

4.36.s: upanīya ca taṃ śiṣyaṃ śaucācāre ca yojayet ..9..
4.36.d: उपनीय च तं शिष्यं शौचाचारे च योजयेत् ..9..
4.36.m: And having initiated that student, he should engage him in purification and right conduct.
He should perform purification according to the rule declared before, and likewise the sipping of water,
Having cleaned teeth and tongue, and having purified bodily impurities.
Having bathed with mantras to the water-deities, carefully having restrained his breaths,
And having performed the standing worship of the sun at both twilights,
And having then performed the fire sacrifice, he should salute the brahmins,
Saying: 'I of such-and-such gotra salute [you].'
For one devoted to salutation and devoted to serving elders,
Life span, fame, strength, and intellect increase day by day.

4.36.s: adhīte guruṇā hūtaḥ prāptaṃ tasmai nivedayet ..
4.36.d: अधीते गुरुणा हूतः प्राप्तं तस्मै निवेदयेत् ..
4.36.m: Called by the guru, he studies; he should offer to him what he has received;
In action, mind, and speech, he should always act for his welfare.
Those who should be taught are: one who asks out of righteousness, not for wealth; the virtuous, the trustworthy, the giver of knowledge, and the giver of wealth.
[and those who are] capable, grateful, pure, free from malice, and free from envy. (15)
He should wear a girdle, a staff, a sacred thread, and an antelope skin;
he should beg alms for his subsistence among irreproachable brahmins. (16)
For a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya, at the beginning, middle, and end,
the begging of alms should respectively be marked by the word bhavat. (17)
Restraining his speech and permitted by his teacher, he should eat his food without despising it;
he should not eat food provided by a single person, [except that] he may eat [it] at a śrāddha and in times of distress. (18)
Overeating produces unhealthiness, shortens life, and bars heaven;
it destroys merit and is hated by the world; therefore, one should avoid it. (19)
The best among twice-born should nowhere eat twice during a single day;
knowing the rules of the agnihotra, a twice-born should eat in the evening and morning. (20)
Honey, meat, injury to living beings, gazing at the sun, applying collyrium,
[consorting with] women, stale food, remnants of meals, and slander he must avoid. (21)
The maximum time for initiation for a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya
is up to the sixteenth, the twenty-second, and the twenty-fourth year [respectively]. (22)
Beyond this they are not to be consecrated; they are fallen, devoid of dharma.
By means of the sacrifice called Vrātyastoma one may rid oneself of that fallen state. (23)
One should not enter into relations with those who have fallen from the Sāvitrī. / For the twice-born, the skin [should be] of a black antelope, a ruru deer, and a goat, respectively. (24)

4.36.s: aiṇaṃ ca rauravaṃ vāstaṃ kramāccarma dvijanmanām ..24..
4.36.d: ऐणं च रौरवं वास्तं क्रमाच्चर्म द्विजन्मनाम् ..24..
4.36.m: The skins of the twice-born are, in order, black antelope, deer, and goat.
They should wear, in order, hempen, linen, and woolen garments. / The girdle of a brahmin should be made of muñja grass; of a kṣatriya, bowstring; (25)

4.36.s: dvijasya mekhalā mauṃjī maurvī ca bhujajanmanaḥ ..
4.36.d: द्विजस्य मेखला मौंजी मौर्वी च भुजजन्मनः ..
4.36.m: The girdle of a twice-born is made of muñja grass, and that of the arm-born is of bowstring bowstring-hemp.
it should be threefold, smooth, and even; but that of a vaiśya [should be] made of hemp threads. (25)
In the absence of muñja, it should be made of kuśa grass, aśmantaka, or balvaja,
furnished with one knot, or with three, or with five. (26)
The sacred thread should be, in order, of cotton, hemp, and wool;
it should be three-stranded and twisted upward for the increase of life. (27)
The staff of a brahmin should be of bilva or palāśa; of a king,
of nyagrodha or a young branch [of badara]; of a vaiśya, of pīlu or udumbara. (28)
In height, it should reach up to the crown of the head, to the forehead, or to the nose;
the staff for a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should have intact bark and not be marred by fire. (29)
Having circumambulated the fire from left to right and worshiped the sun,
equipped with a staff, skin, and sacred thread, he should beg alms as prescribed. (30)
Beginning with his mother, mother's sister, sister, and father's sister,
these should be begged from first; he should utter the solicitation to them. (31)
As long as he studies the Veda, observing the Vedic observances,
so long should he remain a student; thereafter, having bathed, he should become a householder. (32)
This [student] is declared to be the upakurvāṇa; the second among them is the naiṣṭhika.
He should remain in the teacher's house for as long as his life lasts. (33)
He who, having entered the householder stage, again observes student celibacy,
is neither an ascetic nor a forest hermit; he is excluded from all life stages. (34)
A twice-born should not remain even for a single day without an āśrama;

4.36.s: āśramaṃ tu vinā tiṣṭhanprāyaścittī yato hi saḥ ..35..
4.36.d: आश्रमं तु विना तिष्ठन्प्रायश्चित्ती यतो हि सः ..35..
4.36.m: for one who remains without an āśrama must perform expiation. (35)

4.36.s: japaṃ homaṃ vrataṃ dānaṃ svādhyāyaṃ pitṛtarpaṇam..
4.36.d: जपं होमं व्रतं दानं स्वाध्यायं पितृतर्पणम्..
4.36.m: Recitation, oblations, vows, gifts, personal study, and libations to the ancestors—
performing [these] while fallen from his āśrama, he does not obtain their fruit. (36)
The girdle, skin, and staff are the distinguishing marks of the student;
Vedic sacrifices and the like of the householder; [untrimmed] nails and hair of the forest dweller; (37)
the triple staff and so forth are declared to be the marks of the ascetic.
Lacking these marks, one must perform expiation day after day. (38)
A worn-out water pot, staff, sacred thread, and antelope skin—
throwing these into the water, he should take other ones with mantras. (39)
One should perform the ceremony of shaving the hair in the sixteenth year, and in order,
in the twenty-second and twenty-fourth [for the others], for the attainment of the householder state. (40)
Above austerity, sacrifice, vows, and every auspicious rite,
the Śruti alone is the cause of the prosperity of final beatitude for twice-born men. (41)
At the beginning and completion of the Veda, one should always utter the praṇava;
for what is recited without 'oṃ' is fruitless and does not lead to accomplishment. (42)

4.36.s: vedasya vadanaṃ proktaṃ gāyatrī tripadā parā ..
4.36.d: वेदस्य वदनं प्रोक्तं गायत्री त्रिपदा परा ..
4.36.m: The three-footed supreme Gāyatrī is declared to be the mouth of the Veda,
together with the three great vyāhṛtis preceded by the praṇava. (43)
A self-controlled man who repeats this triad a little over a thousand times
outside [the village] every day for a month is released even from a great sin. (44)
He who practices this every day throughout the year with undivided mind,
having a body of ether and a purified self, attains the supreme Brahman. (45)
The three syllables of the oṃkāra, the triad 'bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ',
and the three lines of the Sāvitrī were milked by the three Vedas. (46)
If a Veda-knowing brahmin recites this syllable and this [verse] preceded by the vyāhṛtis
at the two twilights, he is endowed with the merit of the Vedas. (47)
He enjoys ten times the fruit of a ritual sacrifice of prescribed rules.
A sacrifice of recitation is declared to be ten times greater than a prescribed rite. (48)
A whispered recitation is a hundred times that, and a mental recitation a thousand times that. (49)

4.36.s: adhītyavedānvedau vā vedaṃ vā śaktito dvijaḥ ..
4.36.d: अधीत्यवेदान्वेदौ वा वेदं वा शक्तितो द्विजः ..
4.36.m: Having studied the Vedas, or two Vedas, or one Veda according to his ability, a twice-born
reaps the fruit of the gift of the earth filled with gold. (50)
To practice austerity, the best of the twice-born should constantly study the Śruti alone;

4.36.s: śrutyabhyāso hi viprasya paramaṃ tapa ucyate .. 51 ..
4.36.d: श्रुत्यभ्यासो हि विप्रस्य परमं तप उच्यते .. 51 ..
4.36.m: for the study of the Śruti is declared to be the supreme austerity of a brahmin. (51)
He who, having abandoned the study of the Śruti, wishes to read something else,
abandons a milch cow and wishes to milk a village sow. (52)
And when a twice-born performs the initiation of a student and teaches him the Veda,
along with the ritual manuals and secret teachings, the wise know him as an ācārya. (53)
He who teaches a portion of the Śruti, or its auxiliary limbs,
for the sake of a livelihood, is called an upādhyāya by the learned. (54)

4.36.s: yathāvidhi niṣekādi yaḥ karma kurute dvijaḥ ..
4.36.d: यथाविधि निषेकादि यः कर्म कुरुते द्विजः ..
4.36.m: That twice-born who performs rites according to the rule, beginning with the impregnation rite,
and nourishes him with food, is celebrated here as the guru. (55)
He who, being chosen by someone, performs the establishment of the sacred fire, the cooked offerings, and sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma,

4.36.s: yaḥ karoti vṛto yasya sa tasyarttvigihocyate .. 56 ..
4.36.d: यः करोति वृतो यस्य स तस्यर्त्त्विगिहोच्यते .. 56 ..
4.36.m: is called his officiating priest (ṛtvij) here. (56)
An ācārya exceeds ten upādhyāyas, and a father exceeds a hundred ācāryas;
but a mother exceeds a thousand fathers in venerability. (57)

4.36.s: viprāṇāṃ jñānato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ bāhujānāṃ tu vīryataḥ ..
4.36.d: विप्राणां ज्ञानतो ज्यैष्ठ्यं बाहुजानां तु वीर्यतः ..
4.36.m: Seniority among brahmins is through knowledge, but among the arm-born (kṣatriyas) through valor;
among vaiśyas it is through grain and wealth, but among the foot-born (śūdras) through age alone. (58)

4.36.s: yathā dārumayo hastī yathā kṛttimayo mṛgaḥ ..
4.36.d: यथा दारुमयो हस्ती यथा कृत्तिमयो मृगः ..
4.36.m: Just as an elephant made of wood, just as a deer made of leather,
so is a brahmin who does not study: these three merely bear the name. (59)
If a celibate twice-born involuntarily discharges semen in a dream,
he should bathe, worship the sun, and recite three times the verse beginning with 'punar mām'. (60)
In the houses of those devoted to their own duty and engaged in Vedic rites and sacrifices,
a celibate student, restrained, should beg for food daily. (61)
If, without being sick, he does not go begging and does not kindle the sacred fire
for seven nights, he must perform the vow of an avakīrṇin (one who has broken his vow of celibacy). (62)
He should not behave as he pleases within the sight of his guru;
he should not utter his name without an honorific title, even in his absence. (63)
Where censure of the guru takes place, or where there is slander,

4.36.s: śrutī pidhāya vāstheyaṃ yātavyaṃ vā tatonyataḥ .. 64 ..
4.36.d: श्रुती पिधाय वास्थेयं यातव्यं वा ततोन्यतः .. 64 ..
4.36.m: one should either cover both ears or depart from that place to elsewhere. (64)
By slandering the guru one becomes a donkey; a censurer of the guru becomes a dog;
an envious person becomes a petty insect; one who enjoys his property becomes a worm. (65)

4.36.s: nābhivādyā guroḥ patnī spṛṣṭvāṃghrī yuvatī satī ..
4.36.d: नाभिवाद्या गुरोः पत्नी स्पृष्ट्वांघ्री युवती सती ..
4.36.m: A guru's wife who is a young woman should not be greeted by touching her feet
anywhere by one who is twenty years of age and knows virtues and faults. (66)
The nature of women is fickle, and that is remembered as a danger for men;
wise men are never careless with women. (67)
Because they thoroughly subdue both the wise and the unwise,
and bring them under their control like a bird tied with a string. (68)

4.36.s: na mātrā na duhitrā vā na svasraikāṃtaśīlatā ..
4.36.d: न मात्रा न दुहित्रा वा न स्वस्रैकांतशीलता ..
4.36.m: One should not remain in solitude with a mother, a daughter, or a sister;
the senses are powerful in this world and delude even the learned. (69)
Just as one who digs with effort reaches water in the ground,
so the disciple reaches knowledge through service to the guru. (70)
If the sun should rise or set over a celibate student
while sleeping due to negligence, he should fast for the day while reciting [sacred verses]. (71)

4.36.s: sutasya saṃbhave kleśaṃ sahete pitarau ca yat ..
4.36.d: सुतस्य संभवे क्लेशं सहेते पितरौ च यत् ..
4.36.m: The suffering that parents endure at the birth of a son

4.36.s: śakyā varṣaśatenāpi no kartuṃ tasya niṣkṛtiḥ .. 72 ..
4.36.d: शक्या वर्षशतेनापि नो कर्तुं तस्य निष्कृतिः .. 72 ..
4.36.m: cannot be repaid even in a hundred years. (72)
Therefore, one should always do what is pleasing to the two of them and to the guru;

4.36.s: triṣu teṣu sutuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate .. 73 ..
4.36.d: त्रिषु तेषु सुतुष्टेषु तपः सर्वं समाप्यते .. 73 ..
4.36.m: when those three are thoroughly pleased, all austerity is fulfilled. (73)

4.36.s: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate ..
4.36.d: तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते ..
4.36.m: Service to those three is said to be the supreme austerity;
whatever one does while transgressing them can never succeed. (74)
Only by honoring these three may the wise person conquer the three worlds. (75)
He shines in heaven like a god, increasing their delight.

4.36.s: bhūrlokaṃ jananī bhaktyā bhuvarlokaṃ tathā pituḥ ..
4.36.d: भूर्लोकं जननी भक्त्या भुवर्लोकं तथा पितुः ..
4.36.m: Through devotion to his mother [he conquers] the earth; likewise through devotion to his father, the mid-region;
and by serving his guru, the successful man likewise conquers heaven.
This indeed is declared to be the four aims of human life for men,
namely, the satisfaction of these [three]; any other duty is called secondary.

4.36.s: adhītya vedānvedau vā vedaṃ vāpi kramāddvijaḥ ..
4.36.d: अधीत्य वेदान्वेदौ वा वेदं वापि क्रमाद्द्विजः ..
4.36.m: Having studied the Vedas, or two Vedas, or even one Veda in due order,
with his celibate studenthood unswerving, the twice-born should then enter the householder stage.
Celibacy remains unbroken through the grace of the Lord of All;
and the supreme grace of the Lord of All brings about the attainment of Kāśī.

4.38.m: Scratching the head with both hands is not considered auspicious,

By accepting a gift from a king who acts against the scriptures and is greedy,

on the first tithi, on the full-moon day, when an elephant or a camel comes between [teacher and student],

at the Upākarma and the Utsarga, on a boat, on a path, in a tree, in water,

4.38.m: in a proper place and time according to the rule, leads to endless merit.
The giver of land becomes a ruler of a realm; givers of food are happy everywhere;
the giver of water is ever satisfied; the giver of silver becomes handsome.
The giver of a lamp possesses clear eyes; the giver of a cow attains the world of Aryaman.
The giver of gold attains long life, while the giver of sesame seeds will have good offspring.
The giver of a house becomes the master of lofty mansions; the giver of clothing attains the world of the moon.
The giver of a horse attains a divine conveyance; the giver of an ox becomes possessed of fortune.

4.38.m: The giver of a palanquin obtains a good wife, and the giver of an excellent bed also [obtains one].
The giver of grain is ever endowed with prosperity; the giver of fearlessness becomes a ruler.
The giver of sacred knowledge is worshipped in the world of Brahmā; the giver of sacred knowledge is considered the giver of everything.
Even one who, by any means, causes sacred knowledge to be given is equal to him.
He who receives with faith and he who gives with faith—
Both of them become dwellers in heaven; through lack of faith, they fall very low.
A sacrifice is ruined by falsehood; austerity is ruined by conceit;
A gift is ruined by boasting of it; and lifespan is ruined by reviling brahmins.
Perfume, flowers, kuśa grass, a bed, vegetables, meat, milk, curd,
Gems, fish, a house, [and] grain—these should be accepted when offered unasked.
Honey, water, fruit, roots, firewood, and gifts that give reassurance—
These, when brought forward, are to be accepted even from an inferior person.
A slave, a barber, a cowherd, a family friend, a sharecropper,
And one who has dedicated himself—these, among the class of Śūdras, are those whose food may be eaten.
Having thus attained freedom from debt—from the debts born of the gods, seers, and ancestors—
And having transferred all matters everywhere to his son, he should adopt neutrality in the house.
Even at home he may practice spiritual knowledge, or else take refuge in Kāśī;
For liberation comes either through complete knowledge or in the abode of the Lord of the Universe (Viśveśa).
Whence could complete knowledge arise for men in a single birth?
